questions.question: Product of three consecutive odd numbers is 1287. What is the largest of the three numbers?
questions.solution:
Let the 3 numbers be n - 2, n, n + 2

⇒ (n - 2)(n)(n + 2) = 1287

⇒ (n² - 4)(n) = 1287

⇒ n³ - 4n - 1287 = 0

⇒ n = 11 is the only odd number that is the root of above equation

So, the largest number = n + 2 = 11 + 2 = 13

questions.question: 45 men or 60 boys can do a piece of work in 20 days. How many days will 15 men and 20 boys take to complete the work?
questions.solution:
Let the total work be a

Work done by 1 man in 1 day = a/(45 × 20)

Work done by 1 boy in 1 day = a/(60 × 20)

Days needed by 15 men and 20 boys to complete the work = a/{[15a/(45 × 20)] + [20a/(60 × 20)]}

∴ Required days = a/{a/60 + a/60} = a/(a/30) = 30 days

questions.question: The marked price of a shirt is Rs. 1280. If the shirt is being sold for Rs. 900, then what is the discount percentage?
questions.solution:
Given: MP of shirt = Rs. 1280

Selling price of shirt = Rs. 900

Discount = MP - SP = 1280 - 900 = Rs. 380

∴ Discount % = (380/1280) × 100 = 29.68%

questions.question: The ratio of number of cans of orange, pineapple and mixed fruit juices kept in a store is 8 : 9 : 15. If the store sells 25%, 33.33% and 20% of orange, pineapple and mixed fruit juices cans respectively, then what is the ratio of number of cans of these juices in the remaining stock?
questions.solution:
Let the number of cans of orange, pineapple and mixed fruit juices be 8a, 9a and 15a respectively

Number of orange cans sold = (8a)(25/100) = 2a

Number of orange cans left in the stock = 8a - 2a = 6a

Number of pineapple cans sold = (9a)(33.33/100) = 3a

Number of pineapple cans left in the stock = 9a - 3a = 6a

Number of mixed fruit cans sold = (15a)(20/100) = 3a

Number of mixed fruit cans left in the stock = 15a - 3a = 12a

∴ Required ratio = 6a : 6a : 12a = 1 : 1 : 2

questions.question: The ratio of number of boys and girls in a class is 2 : 3. The average weight of boys and girls in the class is 18 kg and 21 kg respectively. What is the average weight (in kgs) of all the boys and girls together?
questions.solution:
Let the number of boys in the class be 2a

Then, the number of girls will be 3a

Given: Average weight of boys in the class = 18 kg

Average weight of girls in the class = 21 kg

Total weight of boys = 18 × 2a = 36a

Total weight of girls = 21 × 3a = 63a

Total weight of the class = 36a + 63a = 99a

Hence, average weight (in kgs) of all the boys and girls together = 99a/(2a + 3a) = 99/5

questions.question: A milk merchant buys 50 litres of milk at the rate of Rs. 40 per litre and mixes 5 litres of water in it. If he sells this mixture at the rate of Rs. 42 per litre, then what is the profit percentage for the dealer?
questions.solution:
Cost price of the milk = 50 × 40 = Rs. 2000

Given: 5 L water is mixed

Total amount of mixture = 50 + 5 = 55 L

Selling price of mixture = 55 × 42 = Rs. 2310

Profit = Rs. (2310 - 2000) = Rs. 310

∴ Profit % = (310/2000) × 100 = 15.5%

questions.question: If A is 6 times of B, then by what percentage is B is less than A?
questions.solution:
We have, a = 6b

Difference between a and b = 6b - b = 5b

∴ % by which B is less than A = (5b/6b) × 100 = 500/6% = 83.33%

questions.question: A runner starts running from a point at 6:00 am with a speed of 8 km/hr. Another racer starts from the same point at 8:30 am in the same direction with a speed of 10 km/hr. At what time of the day (in p.m.) will the second racer will overtake the other runner?
questions.solution:
Let the first runner be A and the second runner be B

Distance covered by A from 6:00 am to 8:30 am = 8 × 2.5 = 20 km

Now, the relative speed of B w.r.t. A = 10 - 8 = 2 km/hr

Taking A to be at rest, B has to cover 20 km to catch up to A

Time taken by B to catch up to A = 20/2 = 10 hours

So, Required time = 8:30 am + 10 hours = 6:30 pm

When [x + (1/x)] = 5, then what is the value of [x - (1/x)]?
questions.solution:
Given: [x + (1/x)] = 5

Squaring both sides we get,

⇒ [x + (1/x)]² = 25

⇒ x² + 1/x² = 25 - 2 = 23 ----(i)

Now, [x - (1/x)]² = x² + 1/x² - 2

⇒ [x - (1/x)]² = x² + 1/x² - 2

Substituting value of x² + 1/x² = 23, we get

⇒ [x - (1/x)]² = 23 - 2

∴ [x - (1/x)] = ± √21

questions.question: If x = (√2 + 1)/(√2 - 1), then what is the value of (x⁵ + x⁴ + x² + x)/x³ ?
questions.solution:
Given: x = (√2 + 1)/(√2 - 1)

Multiplying numerator and denominator by (√2 + 1), we get

⇒ x = (√2 + 1)²/(2 - 1) = 3 + 2√2

To find: (x⁵ + x⁴ + x² + x)/x³ 

⇒ x² + x + 1/x + 1/x²

Calculating x + 1/x, we get

3 + 2√2 + [1/(3 + 2√2)] = [(3 + 2√2)² + 1]/(3 + 2√2)

⇒ (9 + 8 + 12√2 + 1)/(3 + 2√2)

⇒ 6(3 + 2√2)/(3 + 2√2)

⇒ 6

Now, x² + x + 1/x + 1/x² = (x + 1/x)² - 2 + (x + 1/x)

Substituting (x + 1/x) = 6, we get

⇒ 6² - 2 + 6 = 40

∴ the correct option is 1)

questions.question: The point of intersection of all the angle bisector of a triangle is ______ of the triangle.
questions.solution:
If a point lies on the bisector of an angle, then it is equidistant from the sides of the angle.

Hence, the angle bisectors of a triangle intersect at a point called the incenter of the triangle, which is equidistant from the sides of the triangle

questions.question: ABC is an equilateral triangle and P is the orthocenter of the triangle, then what is the value (in degrees) of ∠BPC?
questions.solution:
We, know that the orthocentre is the intersection point of all the altitudes made by the vertices on their corresponding sides

Let take BR and CT as the altitudes

So, in quadrilateral ARPT

∠ATP = ∠ARP = 90°

Since, sum of the opposite angles of quadrilateral = 180°

Hence, it is a cyclic quadrilateral

So, ∠A + ∠BPC = 180°

⇒ ∠BPC = 180° - 60°

∴ ∠BPC = 120°

questions.question: In a triangle ABC, AD is angle bisector of ∠A and AB : AC = 3 : 4. If the area of triangle ABC is 350 cm², then what is the area (in cm²) of triangle ABD?
questions.solution:
We know that, the ratio of the length of the line segment BD to the length of segment DC is equal to the ratio of the length of side AB to the length of side AC

⇒ AC/AB = CD/BD

⇒ CD/BD = 4/3

Altitude of ∆ACD = Altitude of ∆ADB = Altitude of ∆ABC = h

So, their areas would be in the ratio of their bases

⇒ Ar(∆ACD)/ Ar(∆ABD) = 4/3

Let Ar(∆ACD) = 4a and Ar(∆ABD) = 3a

⇒ Ar(∆ACD) + Ar(∆ABD) = Ar(∆ABC)

⇒ 4a + 3a = 350

⇒ 7a = 350

⇒ a = 50

So, area (in cm2) of triangle ABD = 3a = 150 cm²

questions.question: A boat is sailing towards a lighthouse of height 20√3 m at a certain speed. The angle of elevation of the top of the lighthouse changes from 30° to 60° in 10 seconds. What is the time taken (in seconds) by the boat to reach the lighthouse from its initial position?
questions.solution:
Let the point where the angle of elevation of the boat is 60°be A

And the point where the angle of elevation of the boat is 30°be B

Also, let the top of lighthouse be O and bottom be C

Given: height of lighthouse = 20√3 m

In ∆AOC

⇒ tan60° = 20√3/BC

⇒ √3 = 20√3/BC

⇒ BC = 20 m

In ∆AOC

⇒ tan30° = 20√3/AC

⇒ 1/√3 = 20√3/AC

⇒ AC = 60 m

Now, time taken to cover AB = 10 sec

So, speed of boat = (60 - 20)/10 = 4m/s

∴ Time taken by the boat to go from A to C = 60/4 = 15 seconds

questions.question: What should be the least number of runs that Pujara must have scored in total (runs can only be integers)?
